title: SIT-Eval: Situation-Based Interactive Turn-by-Turn Evaluation of Conversational Agents

paragraphs.en: The rapid proliferation of conversational AI agents necessitates evaluation methods that assess performance across diverse dialogue scenarios, utilizing multiple situational criteria, as appropriate behavior depends on context and encompasses various aspects. Existing dialogue benchmarks typically use static natural conversations, which underrepresent rare situations—a critical safety gap, as low-probability events become frequent failures at production scale. However, limited sample sizes force a choice: either maintain natural dialogues for realism or turn to adaptive situation sampling for comprehensive yet statistically reliable coverage. We introduce SIT-Eval, an adjustable framework for evaluating situation-based conversational agents. We formalize an agent’s desired behavior as situational rules: if situation is P, follow rules Q . At each conversation turn, an LLM-interlocutor enacts a uniformly sampled situation. A context-aware LLM-judge leverages all conditionally applicable rules as criteria to evaluate the agent’s reply for that situation. The judge is validated using human-verified synthetic golden dialogues. Benchmarking 8 LLMs on 1292 conversation turns reveals failure modes hidden by aggregate metrics: models with similar overall scores vary widely in their adherence to individual rules. All models struggle most with ambiguity clarification and Socratic questioning.
paragraphs.zh: 对话式人工智能智能体的迅速普及，需要采用能够评估其在多样化对话场景中表现的评价方法，并运用多种情境标准，因为恰当的行为取决于具体语境且涵盖多个方面。 现有的对话基准测试通常使用静态的自然对话，这无法充分反映罕见情境——这是一个关键的安全漏洞，因为在生产规模下，低概率事件会演变为频繁出现的失败。 然而，有限的样本量迫使我们做出选择：要么保留自然对话以确保真实性，要么转向自适应情境采样，以实现全面且统计可靠的覆盖。 我们提出了 SIT-Eval，一个用于评估基于情境的对话式智能体的可调节框架。 我们将智能体期望的行为形式化为情境规则：如果情境为 P，则遵循规则 Q。 在每次对话回合中，一个 LLM 对话者会执行一个均匀采样的情境。 一个具备语境感知能力的 LLM 评判者会利用所有条件适用的规则作为标准，来评估智能体在该情境下的回复。 该评判者通过经人类验证的合成黄金对话进行验证。 对 8 个 LLM 在 1292 次对话回合中的基准测试揭示了聚合指标所掩盖的失败模式：整体分数相似模型在遵守具体规则方面的差异显著。 所有模型在处理歧义澄清和苏格拉底式提问时都存在最大困难。

paragraphs.en: We introduce SIT-Eval ( Sit uation-Based I nteractive T urn-by-Turn Eval uation), an adjustable framework that resolves this trade-off through controlled, interactive evaluation. SIT-Eval formalizes an agent’s desired behavior as situational rules of the form if situation is P, follow rules Q . At each conversation turn, an LLM-interlocutor enacts a uniformly sampled situation from a predefined action space, ensuring both common and rare scenarios receive equal statistical representation. A context-aware LLM-judge then evaluates the agent’s reply against all conditionally applicable rules, producing granular turn-by-turn assessments rather than a single opaque score for the entire dialogue. Crucially, the judge undergoes rigorous validation on human-verified synthetic “golden” dialogues before deployment, addressing the reliability concerns identified in prior work Bavaresco et al. (2025) ; Zheng et al. (2023) .
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出 SIT-Eval（情境化交互式回合评估），一个可通过受控的交互式评估来解决这一权衡问题的可调节框架。 SIT-Eval 将智能体期望的行为形式化为情境规则：如果情境为 P，则遵循规则 Q。 在每次对话回合中，一个 LLM 对话者会从预定义的动作空间中均匀采样一个情境，确保常见和罕见情境都能获得均等的统计代表性。 随后，一个具备上下文感知能力的 LLM 评判者会根据所有条件适用的规则评估智能体的回复，从而生成精细的回合级评估，而非对整个对话给出单一的不透明分数。 关键在于，该评判者在部署前需基于经人类验证的合成“黄金”对话进行严格验证，以解决先前研究（Bavaresco 等人，2025；Zheng 等人，2023）中识别出的可靠性问题。

paragraphs.en: A situation-based evaluation framework with uniform action sampling. Unlike existing benchmarks that inherit the skewed situation distribution of natural dialogues Macina et al. (2023) ; Chevalier et al. (2024) , SIT-Eval assigns equal probability to all predefined interlocutor actions. This design choice ensures statistically significant sample sizes for rare situations (e.g., student distraction, repeated confusion) that would otherwise require prohibitively large natural datasets to evaluate reliably.

paragraphs.en: A set of 12 expert-crafted pedagogical rules operationalizing Socratic tutoring. Developed in collaboration with professional methodologists, these rules define unambiguous behavioral criteria across seven categories (Socratic questioning, ambiguity clarification, error handling, etc.), enabling reproducible evaluation of tutoring agents.

paragraphs.en: Empirical benchmarking revealing hidden failure modes. Evaluating 8 LLMs across 1292 conversation turns, we find that models with similar overall adherence scores vary dramatically in per-rule performance—a finding obscured by aggregate metrics. All models struggle most with ambiguity clarification and Socratic questioning, identifying specific targets for improvement.
paragraphs.zh: 经验性基准测试揭示了隐藏的失效模式。 通过对 8 个大型语言模型在 1292 轮对话中的评估，我们发现，尽管这些模型的总体遵循分数相似，但在每条规则上的表现却差异显著——这一发现被聚合指标所掩盖。 所有模型在处理模糊性澄清和苏格拉底式提问时都存在最大困难，这为改进指明了具体方向。

paragraphs.en: By enabling the statistically reliable assessment of agent behavior across both standard and edge scenarios, SIT-Eval advances the development of safer and more effective conversational AI systems.
paragraphs.zh: SIT-Eval 通过实现对标准场景和边缘场景中智能体行为的统计可靠评估，推动了更安全、更高效的对话式人工智能系统的发展。

paragraphs.en: Our study builds on three converging research areas: the use of LLMs as evaluators, benchmarks for AI tutors, and simulated dialogues for multi-turn evaluation. paragraphs.en: The LLM-as-judge paradigm has rapidly advanced. Zheng et al. (2023) demonstrated that GPT-4 aligns well with human preferences in the Chatbot Arena, confirming its potential for scalable evaluation while also revealing systematic biases, including a preference for verbosity and self-enhancement. Ensemble approaches mitigate these issues but increase cost; Tang et al. (2025) reduced this overhead by distilling a single evaluator from multiple judges. Despite progress, reliability remains a concern. Tan et al. (2025) introduced JudgeBench to stress-test judges, demonstrating that even GPT-4 struggles with difficult comparisons, which proves that human-alignment alone is insufficient. We address this gap via a two-phase validation: calibrating our LLM-judge on “golden” dialogues with known outcomes before deployment. This ensures it can reliably distinguish correct from incorrect tutor behaviors, going beyond prior works that accept LLM judgments at face value.
paragraphs.zh: 将大型语言模型用作评判者的范式已迅速发展。Zheng 等人 (2023) 的研究表明，GPT-4 在“聊天机器人竞技场”中能够很好地与人类偏好保持一致，这证实了其在可扩展评估方面的潜力，同时也揭示了系统性的偏见，包括对冗长表达和自我提升的偏好。 集成方法可以缓解这些问题，但也会增加成本；Tang 等人 (2025) 通过从多个评判者中蒸馏出单个评估器，降低了这种额外开销。 尽管取得了进展，可靠性仍然是一个问题。Tan 等人 (2025) 引入了 JudgeBench 来对评判者进行压力测试，结果表明，即使是 GPT-4 也难以处理复杂的比较任务，这证明了仅靠与人类偏好保持一致是远远不够的。 我们通过一个两阶段验证流程来解决这一差距：在部署之前，使用结果已知的“黄金”对话对我们的 LLM 评判者进行校准。 这确保了它能够可靠地区分正确的和错误的导师行为，超越了那些直接接受 LLM 判断结果的前期研究。

paragraphs.en: Tutor evaluation requires formulating criteria beyond generic fluency. Pauzi et al. (2025) demonstrated that standard NLG metrics overlook pedagogical subtleties; their rubric revealed that LLM-judges grasp surface qualities but overlook skills such as scaffolding and mistake remediation. Similarly, Maurya et al. (2025) reported a low correlation with human ratings on pedagogical dimensions in MRBench, urging the need for more specialized evaluators. We respond by validating and iteratively refining our judgment on rule-specific golden dialogues where each “good” vs. “bad” turn is predefined. Measuring per-rule accuracy enables retraining or prompt adjustments until high fidelity is achieved, unlike previous benchmarks, which report only post-hoc correlations.
paragraphs.zh: 导师评估需要制定超越通用流利度的标准。Pauzi 等人 (2025) 指出，标准的自然语言生成指标忽视了教学中的细微差别；他们的评分表显示，大型语言模型评判者虽然能理解表层特征，却忽略了脚手架搭建和错误纠正等技能。同样地，Maurya 等人 (2025) 报告称，在 MRBench 中，模型在教學维度上与人类评分的相关性较低，因此呼吁需要更专业的评估方法。 我们的回应是，通过验证并迭代优化我们对特定规则黄金对话的判断来实现这一目标，在这些对话中，每个“好”与“坏”的回合都已预先定义。 按规则测量准确性使得我们可以重新训练或调整提示，直到达到高保真度；这与仅报告事后相关性的先前基准测试不同。

paragraphs.en: Simulated dialogues capture dynamic tutoring more effectively. Shi et al. (2025) proposed EducationQ, where LLMs play teacher, student, and evaluator, revealing that teaching quality does not scale linearly with model size. Yet its student is cooperative, and the evaluation is holistic. We introduce an LLM-interlocutor that systematically triggers diverse situations to test each pedagogical rule. Other works focus narrowly, e.g., Liu et al. (2024b) analyzed code-switching in language learning but only verified the presence of a tactic. Our benchmark instead provides comprehensive situation coverage to test an agent’s performance. Moreover, equal probability weighting for both standard and rare situations enables a balanced assessment of both routine and rare scenarios, ensuring that the agent’s robustness is measured relative to a set of predefined situations and rules.
paragraphs.zh: 模拟对话能更有效地捕捉动态辅导过程。Shi 等人 （2025）提出了 EducationQ，其中大语言模型同时扮演教师、学生和评估者的角色，研究结果表明教学质量的提升并非与模型规模呈线性关系。 然而，其学生角色具有合作性，且评估过程是全面的。 我们引入了一种大语言模型对话者，它能系统性地触发多种情境，以测试每一条教学规则。 其他研究则聚焦于狭窄的领域，例如 Liu 等人 （2024b）分析了语言学习中的代码转换现象，但仅验证了某种策略的存在性。 相比之下，我们的基准测试提供了全面的情境覆盖，用于评估智能体的表现。 此外，对常规情境和罕见情境赋予相等的概率权重，能够实现对两者均衡的评估，从而确保智能体的稳健性是相对于一组预定义情境和规则来衡量的。

paragraphs.en: Benchmarks like TutorEval ( Chevalier et al., 2024 ) frame tutoring as QA: GPT-4 grades answers to textbook questions using key-point references. For factual accuracy, this overlooks dialogue dynamics, such as guiding or handling follow-ups. It also relies on reference-based grading, which is unsuitable for open-ended exchanges. Similarly, TutorBench ( Srinivasa et al., 2025 ) assesses tutoring capabilities through direct question-answering or with short dialogues featuring a fixed single-turn history, which limits its ability to capture the complexity of extended, multi-turn interactions. Instead, our method evaluates the quality of the process: tutor adherence to pedagogical principles across full multi-turn interactions.
paragraphs.zh: 像 TutorEval（Chevalier 等人，2024）这样的基准测试将辅导视为问答任务：GPT-4 根据关键要点参考来批改教科书问题的答案。 在事实准确性方面，这种方法忽略了对话动态，例如引导或处理后续问题。 它还依赖基于参考的评分方式，而这种方式并不适用于开放式交流。 类似地，TutorBench（Srinivasa 等人，2025）通过直接问答或包含固定单轮历史记录的简短对话来评估辅导能力，这限制了其捕捉长期多轮互动复杂性的能力。 相反，我们的方法评估的是过程的质量：即辅导者在完整的多轮互动中是否遵循了教学原则。

paragraphs.en: Macina et al. (2025) introduced MathTutorBench, assessing hint-giving, scaffolding, and Socratic questioning. Yet its fragmented datasets and short dialogues hinder comprehensive evaluation. It also uses static dialogues, where (a) tutors respond to pre-existing conversation parts, whose token distribution may unpredictably affect the agent’s answer generation at the turn under evaluation, and (b) scenario diversity is limited by the natural frequency, preventing comprehensive situation coverage. Our dynamic, situation-diverse dialogues overcome both. Moreover, MathTutorBench’s BLEU-based scoring for Socratic questioning is overly rigid, which explains the universally low scores. Anonymous (2025) proposed IndirectScore, which utilizes surprisal to assess the indirectness of questions. However, it only addresses one aspect of Socratic dialogue and aligns with humans at 71%. Our validated judge achieves 81% accuracy on this rule and 92.6% overall, offering a broader and more reliable assessment. MathDial ( Macina et al., 2023 ) offers static tutoring dialogues, but its single student prompt restricts behavioral diversity; metrics such as sBLEU and BERTScore remain too stringent for open-ended turns, and annotations are coarse. Proposed Success@k and Telling@k emphasize final answers, missing premature step revelation, a behavior that SIT-Eval can evaluate. The authors themselves note that defining reliable tutor metrics remains unresolved.

sents.zh: 我们经过验证的评判器在该规则上的准确率达到 81%，整体准确率为 92.6%，提供了更广泛、更可靠的评估。

sents.en: MathDial ( Macina et al., 2023 ) offers static tutoring dialogues, but its single student prompt restricts behavioral diversity; metrics such as sBLEU and BERTScore remain too stringent for open-ended turns, and annotations are coarse.
sents.zh: MathDial（Macina 等人，2023）提供了静态的辅导对话，但其单一的学生提示限制了行为多样性；sBLEU 和 BERTScore 等指标对于开放式回合仍然过于严格，且标注较为粗略。

sents.en: Proposed Success@k and Telling@k emphasize final answers, missing premature step revelation, a behavior that SIT-Eval can evaluate.
sents.zh: 提出的 Success@k 和 Telling@k 强调最终答案，却忽略了过早揭示步骤的行为，而 SIT-Eval 能够评估这种行为。

sents.en: The authors themselves note that defining reliable tutor metrics remains unresolved.
sents.zh: 作者本人也指出，定义可靠的导师评估指标仍是一个未解决的问题。

paragraphs.en: Similar issues arise beyond education. Our dynamic, turn-level situation-based framework generalizes across domains.

paragraphs.en: In existing benchmarks, dialogue situations 𝒮 \mathcal{S} are typically derived from collected human-expert dialogues, where the interlocutor may be a real person or an LLM. Segmenting these dialogues at various points yields situation categories (e.g., scaffolding, error correction). Given a tutor as a black-box mapping 𝒯 : 𝒮 → 𝒴 \mathcal{T}:\mathcal{S}\to\mathcal{Y} from situations to textual responses, benchmarking estimates a performance score as the proportion of situations in which the tutor’s response matches the ground-truth behavior recorded by human experts.
paragraphs.zh: 在现有的基准测试中，对话情境 𝒮 \mathcal{S} 通常源自收集的人类专家对话，其中对话对象可能是真人或大型语言模型（LLM）。 在这些对话的不同位置进行分割，可以得出不同的情境类别（例如，搭建框架、错误纠正）。 假设导师是一个黑箱映射 𝒯 : 𝒮 → 𝒴 \mathcal{T}:\mathcal{S}\to\mathcal{Y}，将情境映射为文本回应，基准测试通过计算导师的回应与人类专家记录的真实行为相匹配的情境比例来估算性能得分。

paragraphs.en: We propose decoupling the evaluation standard from recorded expert responses and instead grounding it in a set of textual rules ℛ = { R 1 , R 2 , … , R n } \mathcal{R}=\{R_{1},R_{2},\ldots,R_{n}\} that characterize desired agent behavior across situations.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出将评估标准与记录在案的专家回答解耦，转而将其基于一组文本规则 ℛ = { R 1 , R 2 , … , R n } \mathcal{R}=\{R_{1},R_{2},\ldots,R_{n}\}，这些规则用于描述智能体在不同情境下的期望行为。

paragraphs.en: Core Assumption. Each rule R ∈ ℛ R\in\mathcal{R} is a conditional statement: if situation S S occurs, the agent must satisfy criterion C C . We require that C C is unambiguous given the dialogue context, enabling the deterministic classification of rule adherence by both human and LLM evaluators.
paragraphs.zh: 核心假设。 每条规则 R ∈ ℛ（R∈ℛ）都是一条条件陈述：如果情境 S 出现，智能体必须满足标准 C。 我们要求，在对话上下文中，标准 C 的含义必须明确无误，从而使得人类和大型语言模型评估者都能对规则遵守情况进行确定性分类。

paragraphs.en: This formulation assumes: (1) rules are precisely defined with clear positive/negative behaviors; (2) situations are observable from interlocutor actions and context; (3) adherence is binary (follow/violate); (4) conversation history suffices for evaluation. Figure 2 illustrates this framework.
paragraphs.zh: 该公式假设：(1) 规则有明确定义，包含清晰的积极/消极行为；(2) 情况可通过对话者的行为和上下文观察到；(3) 遵守规则是二元的（遵循/违反）；(4) 对话历史足以进行评价。 图 2 展示了这一框架。

paragraphs.en: A situation is a class of dialogue contexts requiring specific agent behavior; each situation triggers one or more rules from ℛ \mathcal{R} . For example, when a student correctly completes a step, applicable rules include praise the student , do not reveal the next step , and ask a leading question .
paragraphs.zh: 情境是一类需要智能体采取特定行为的对话语境；每种情境都会触发规则集 ℛ \mathcal{R} 中的一条或多条规则。 例如，当学生正确完成一个步骤时，适用的规则包括：表扬学生、不透露下一步骤以及提出引导性问题。

paragraphs.en: For the pedagogical domain, we define 12 expert-crafted rules organized into seven categories: Socratic Questioning (Rules 1–3), Ambiguity Clarification (4), Explanation & Adaptation (5), Distraction Handling (6), Emotional Intelligence (7–8), Error Detection (9–10), and Problem Conclusion (11–12). Rule 3 (Socratic Questioning) is particularly challenging to formulate and evaluate. Complete rule definitions, action prompts, and their mappings are available in the code repository.

paragraphs.en: Crucially, the LLM-interlocutor enacts uniformly sampled actions. This design choice offers three advantages: (1) rare situations (e.g., student distraction) receive equal statistical representation as common ones; (2) uniform sampling maximizes entropy, stress-testing the agent with maximally unpredictable interlocutor behavior; (3) given a fixed sample budget, uniform allocation across situations maximizes per-situation coverage.
paragraphs.zh: 至关重要的是，LLM对话者会执行均匀采样的动作。 这一设计选择带来了三个优势：（1）罕见情境（例如学生分心）与常见情境在统计上获得了同等程度的体现；（2）均匀采样能最大化熵值，通过让智能体面对尽可能不可预测的对话者行为来对其进行压力测试；（3）在样本预算固定的情况下，将样本均匀分配给不同情境能够最大化每个情境的覆盖范围。

paragraphs.en: Before deployment, we validate LLM-judges on “golden” dialogues, synthetic conversations with known correct and incorrect agent responses, verified by human experts to ensure actions and responses match their intended prompts.
paragraphs.zh: 在部署之前，我们会使用“黄金”对话来验证 LLM-判断者。这些对话是合成生成的，其中包含已知正确和错误的智能体响应，并由人类专家进行核实，以确保其行动和响应与预期提示相匹配。

paragraphs.en: At each turn with action A A , the judge receives all applicable rules ℛ A \mathcal{R}_{A} and classifies the agent’s response as following or violating each rule. We compare judgments to ground-truth labels and compute: (1) overall accuracy, (2) per-rule accuracy, (3) statistical significance versus random baseline (Cohen’s h h ), and (4) false positive/negative balance. Judge prompts appear in Appendix A.3 .
paragraphs.zh: 在每个回合中，当执行动作 A 时，裁判会收到所有适用的规则 ℛ A \mathcal{R}_{A}，并对智能体的响应进行分类，判断其是遵循还是违反了每条规则。 我们将裁判结果与真实标签进行比较，并计算：(1) 总体准确率，(2) 每条规则的准确率，(3) 与随机基线相比的统计显著性（Cohen’s h h），以及 (4) 假阳性/假阴性平衡。 裁判提示词见附录 A.3。

paragraphs.en: We conducted a series of experiments to demonstrate the capabilities of the SIT-Eval framework. Our goals were to:
paragraphs.zh: 我们进行了一系列实验，以展示 SIT-Eval 框架的能力。我们的目标是：

paragraphs.en: Generate a set of golden dialogues and estimate its noise level using human expert verification.
paragraphs.zh: 生成一组黄金对话，并使用人类专家验证来评估其噪声水平。

paragraphs.en: Validate the LLM-judge against a set of golden dialogues to ensure its reliability.
paragraphs.zh: 使用一组黄金对话来验证 LLM-判断器，以确保其可靠性。

paragraphs.en: Benchmark state-of-the-art AI tutors to evaluate their pedagogical performance, conducting cross-comparison of the obtained results with the previous work.
paragraphs.zh: 对基准领域的顶尖人工智能导师进行评估，以检验其教学表现，并将所得结果与先前的研究进行跨比较分析。

paragraphs.en: Analyze the results to pinpoint the tutors’ strengths and weaknesses with respect to our expert-crafted predefined pedagogical rules.
paragraphs.zh: 分析结果，以明确智能体在遵循我们专家制定的预定义教学规则方面的优势与不足。

paragraphs.en: To maximize reproducibility, we used a sample of 500 problems from the well-known, openly available GSM8K dataset ( Cobbe et al., 2021 ) , which comprises 8,500 grade school math word problems. Each problem includes a golden solution and requires multi-step reasoning, making it well-suited for evaluating pedagogical interactions. The sample of 500 problems was used for golden dialogue generation and LLM-judge validation. The first 170 problems from the sample were used for the actual benchmark.
paragraphs.zh: 为最大限度地确保可重复性，我们使用了来自知名且公开可用的 GSM8K 数据集（Cobbe 等人，2021）的 500 道问题样本，该数据集包含 8,500 道小学数学应用题。 每道题都附有标准答案，并需要多步骤推理，因此非常适合用于评估教学互动。 这 500 道问题的样本被用于生成标准对话以及 LLM 判官验证。 该样本中的前 170 道题被用于实际的基准测试。

paragraphs.en: We generated 500 golden dialogues using Claude Sonnet 4.5 for all components (LLM-student, LLM-tutor, LLM-judge), with uniform action sampling and a 50% split between rule-following and rule-violating tutor responses. Three human experts annotated a sample of 100 dialogues (1,292 turn-level items), identifying only 0.85% as noisy, which confirms that the golden dialogues provide a reliable ground truth. Example dialogues appear in Appendices C and D .
paragraphs.zh: 我们使用 Claude Sonnet 4.5 为所有组件（LLM-学生、LLM-导师、LLM-评判者）生成了 500 条黄金对话，其中采用了统一的动作采样，并将导师的回应按规则遵循与规则违反的比例进行 50% 的划分。 三位人类专家对 100 条对话样本（共 1,292 个轮次级条目）进行了标注，仅识别出 0.85% 的噪声内容，这证实了这些黄金对话提供了可靠的基准事实。 示例对话见附录 C 和 D。

paragraphs.en: To enable cross-comparison with prior work, we evaluated multiple AI tutors on the SIT-Eval framework. Following Macina et al. (2025) , we included the same specialized tutoring models from MathTutorBench: Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-AWQ Meta (2024) , Llemma-7B-Science-Tutor Chevalier et al. (2024) , Qwen-2.5-7B-SocraticLM Jain (2025) , Qwen-2.5-Math-7B-Instruct Yang et al. (2024) , and LearnLM Team et al. (2025) . We additionally benchmarked state-of-the-art general-purpose models: Claude Sonnet 4.5 Anthropic (2025) , GPT-5 OpenAI (2025) , and Gemini 2.5 Pro Google (2025) .
paragraphs.zh: 为了能够与先前的工作进行跨研究比较，我们在 SIT-Eval 框架上评估了多个 AI 智能体。遵循 Macina 等人（2025）的研究，我们纳入了 MathTutorBench 中的相同专业辅导模型：Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-AWQ Meta（2024）、Llemma-7B-Science-Tutor Chevalier 等人（2024）、Qwen-2.5-7B-SocraticLM Jain（2025）、Qwen-2.5-Math-7B-Instruct Yang 等人（2024）以及 LearnLM Team 等人（2025）。此外，我们还对当前最先进的通用模型进行了基准测试：Claude Sonnet 4.5 Anthropic（2025）、GPT-5 OpenAI（2025）以及 Gemini 2.5 Pro Google（2025）。

paragraphs.en: Self-preference bias . A potential concern is that Claude, serving as the judge, might favor its own responses. Recent work shows that while strong LLM evaluators exhibit self-preference, when strong models favor themselves, they are mostly objectively correct Chen et al. (2025) . Importantly, structured evaluation with step-by-step reasoning significantly reduces harmful self-preference bias Chen et al. (2025) , which is precisely the approach we adopt, requiring the judge to provide explicit rationales for each of the 12 rules. To empirically verify judge neutrality, we re-evaluated the benchmark dialogues of the top two models (Claude and Gemini) using Gemini 2.5 Flash as an independent judge. The ranking remained unchanged: Claude scored 84.3% vs. Gemini’s 79.0%, preserving the original 5-point gap. This cross-validation confirms that our results reflect genuine performance differences rather than self-preference artifacts.

(2025)，而这正是我们所采用的方法：要求评判者为 12 条规则中的每一条提供明确的推理依据。 为了实证验证评判者的中立性，我们使用 Gemini 2.5 Flash 作为独立评判者，重新评估了排名前两名的模型（Claude 和 Gemini）的基准对话数据集。 排名保持不变：Claude 得分为 84.3%，而 Gemini 得分为 79.0%，两者之间原有的 5 个百分点差距得以保留。 这种交叉验证证实，我们的结果反映了真实的性能差异，而非自我偏好造成的偏差。

paragraphs.en: Discussion . Three clear patterns emerged from benchmarking. First, models typically guess rather than ask for clarification. All models demonstrated low adherence to rule 4 (Ambiguity Clarification): 2–47%, average 11%. No model exceeded 47% even with explicit instructions. From a pedagogical perspective, clarification-seeking is valuable: one skill we want students to develop is being unambiguous in their communication. This suggests instruction-tuning datasets could benefit from more targeted examples of ambiguity clarification behavior.
paragraphs.zh: 讨论。 基准测试揭示了三个清晰的模式。 首先，模型通常倾向于猜测，而不是请求澄清。 所有模型在规则 4（模糊性澄清）上的遵守率都很低：2–47%，平均为 11%。 即使有明确指示，也没有任何模型的遵守率超过 47%。 从教学角度来看，主动寻求澄清很有价值：我们希望学生培养的一项技能，就是在沟通中表达清晰、避免歧义。 这表明，指令微调数据集或许可以从更针对模糊性澄清行为的示例中受益。

paragraphs.en: Third, providing explicit rule specifications improved performance for 4 of 5 general-purpose models (average +7%). This is expected: when evaluation criteria are explicitly stated in the prompt, models tend to follow those criteria more closely. The practical implication: deployment prompts should include explicit behavioral specifications, not just task descriptions. However, GPT-5 anomalously decreased from 75% (base) to 52% (full), primarily due to a technical issue: it sporadically produced empty responses (265 empty responses out of 650 total turns), which is unexpected for the state-of-the-art instruction-following model according to Chiang et al. (2024) . In the meantime, the GPT-5 tutor equipped with the base prompt produced empty responses only in 17 turns.

paragraphs.en: Task-specific models behaved as expected. Qwen-Math performed poorly (17%) because it is a solver, not a tutor. Additionally, Qwen-Math failed on 55 of 100 dialogues due to contaminating the message history with lengthy gibberish, which exceeded its maximum context length. Llemma-Science-Tutor (29%) showed decent Emotional Intelligence, Socratic Questioning and Explanation, given its QA+explain training rather than collaborative problem-solving. However, it produced empty or whitespace responses in 5 turns. SocraticLM (64%) reflected the original characteristics of the SocraTeach Liu et al. (2024a) dataset: it was strong on most rules, except for the ambiguity clarification rule (2%), as the dataset lacks such examples.
paragraphs.zh: 任务特定模型的表现符合预期。 Qwen-Math 表现不佳（17%），因为它是一个解题器，而非导师。 此外，Qwen-Math 在 100 段对话中失败了 55 次，原因是它将冗长的无意义内容混入消息历史，超出了其最大上下文长度限制。 Llemma-Science-Tutor（29%）展现出不错的同理心、苏格拉底式提问和解释能力，这与其基于“问答+解释”的训练方式而非协作式问题解决有关。 然而，它在 5 轮对话中给出了空回复或仅含空白字符的回复。 SocraticLM（64%）反映了 SocraTeach Liu et al. (2024a) 数据集的原始特征：它在大多数规则上表现良好，但在消除歧义规则上仅为 2%，因为该数据集缺乏此类示例。

paragraphs.en: This paper introduces SIT-Eval, a novel framework for dynamic, situation-based, and fine-grained evaluation of conversational agents. Our approach utilizes an LLM-based interlocutor with an equal probability distribution across actions to systematically test the agent’s adherence to predefined behavioral rules across diverse situations, complemented by a rigorously validated LLM judge for reliable turn-by-turn evaluation.
paragraphs.zh: 本文介绍了 SIT-Eval，一个用于对话智能体的动态、情境化且精细评估的新框架。 我们的方法采用了一个基于大语言模型（LLM）的对话伙伴，该伙伴在各动作间具有均等概率分布，从而系统性地测试智能体在不同情境下对预设行为规则的遵循程度，并辅以经过严格验证的 LLM 评判者，以实现可靠的逐轮评估。

paragraphs.en: The ability to tune the probability distributions for action selection also enables researchers to create customized benchmarks tailored to their specific needs. The customizable probability distributions would allow researchers to create evaluation scenarios ranging from natural frequency distributions to uniform distributions, ensuring equal coverage of rare situations and providing unprecedented control over situation diversity. By providing systematic, controlled, and naturalistic evaluation across all situations, both common and rare, SIT-Eval addresses critical gaps in current evaluation methodologies.
paragraphs.zh: 调整动作选择的概率分布的能力也使研究人员能够创建符合其特定需求的定制基准。 可定制的分布概率将允许研究人员创建从自然频率分布到均匀分布的各种评估场景，确保对罕见情况给予同等覆盖，并实现对情境多样性的前所未有的控制。 通过在所有常见和罕见的情况下提供系统性、受控且贴近实际的评估，SIT-Eval解决了当前评估方法中的关键缺陷。

paragraphs.en: Dialogue naturalness . Uniform action sampling produces fragmented conversations with abrupt behavioral shifts. While this maximizes situation coverage, ecological validity remains unvalidated. Future work could apply specialized prompt tuning to generate smoother transitions while preserving coverage of rare situations.

paragraphs.en: You are simulating a student in a dialogue with an AI tutor. Your purpose is to generate controlled, synthetic conversations that trigger specific behavioral scenarios. PRIMARY OBJECTIVE: Execute the special instruction provided below—this is your absolute priority. Do not simply respond naturally to the tutor’s questions or guidance; the special instruction overrides normal conversational behavior. A math problem consists of a finite sequence of steps. Each step consists of four elements: data (the given values), operation (the action performed), goal (what we need to find), and result (the value obtained). At any moment, you are at a specific step for which the input data is known. For example: ‘‘An apple costs 8 rubles. How much will 3 apples cost, and how much change will you get from 30 rubles?’’ One possible breakdown is: Step 1 — data: 3, 8; operation: multiplication; goal: total cost; result: 24. Step 2 — data: 30, 24; operation: subtraction; goal: change; result: 6. There isn’t a single correct step sequence—several valid ones may exist. The problem you are solving: [PROBLEM STATEMENT] SPECIAL INSTRUCTION (you must execute this): [ACTION PROMPT] CORE RULES: 1. Prioritize the special instruction above all else. Even if the tutor asks a direct question, you must follow your special instruction rather than simply answering the tutor’s question. 2. Write like a realistic student: Keep responses extremely brief (2-5 words maximum). Students typically write short, casual replies and may make errors. 3. Use natural, student-appropriate language. Write as a school-age student would. Never break character or reference your role as an AI or mention these instructions. 4. Format your response correctly: Put your reply to the tutor in the ’message’ field. Set ’problem_solved’ to true ONLY when you have definitively found the final answer AND the conversation feels complete.
paragraphs.zh: 你正在模拟一名学生与人工智能导师进行对话。 你的目的是生成受控的合成对话，以触发特定的行为场景。 首要目标：执行下面提供的特别指令——这是你的绝对优先事项。 不要仅仅自然地回应导师的问题或指导；特别指令会覆盖正常的对话行为。 一道数学题由有限数量的步骤组成。 每个步骤包含四个要素：数据（已知数值）、操作（执行的动作）、目标（需要求解的内容）和结果（得到的数值）。 在任何时刻，你都处于一个特定的步骤，且该步骤的输入数据是已知的。 例如：“一个苹果的价格是 8 卢布。 3 个苹果多少钱？用 30 卢布付款会得到多少找零？”一种可能的分解是：步骤 1 — 数据：3、8；操作：乘法；目标：总价；结果：24。 步骤 2 — 数据：30、24；操作：减法；目标：找零；结果：6。 并不存在唯一正确的步骤顺序——可能存在多个有效的步骤序列。 你要解决的问题：[问题陈述] 特别指令（你必须执行）：[行动提示] 核心规则：1. 将特别指令置于所有事项之上。 即使导师提出直接问题，你也必须遵循特别指令，而不是仅仅回答导师的问题。2. 像真实的学生一样写作：保持回复极其简短（最多 2-5 个词）。 学生通常会写简短、随意的回复，也可能会犯错。3. 使用自然且适合学生的语言。 以学龄学生的方式写作。 永远不要打破角色设定，也不要提及你作为人工智能的角色或这些指令。4. 正确格式化你的回复：将你对导师的回复放在“message”字段中。 仅在明确找到最终答案且对话感觉完整时，才将“problem_solved”设为 true。

paragraphs.en: A minimal pedagogical instruction adapted from MathTutorBench’s Scaffolding and Pedagogy guidelines:

paragraphs.en: You are an experienced math teacher, and you are going to respond to a student in a useful and caring way. The student is trying to solve the following problem: [PROBLEM STATEMENT] Be a friendly, supportive tutor. Guide the student to solve the problem, gently nudging them on task if they stray. Ask guiding questions to help your students take incremental steps toward the solution and understanding big concepts. Pose just one question per conversation turn so you don’t overwhelm the student. Wrap up the conversation once the student has solved the problem. Check the correctness of the student’s solution to the problem. Your goal is to help students reach the final answer through their own thinking. Do not reveal solution steps directly.

paragraphs.en: The SIT-Eval framework is designed to be domain-agnostic. This section provides guidelines for researchers adapting our methodology to evaluate conversational agents in domains beyond mathematical tutoring.

paragraphs.en: Effective rules should capture specific, observable behaviors rather than abstract qualities. For example, instead of "be empathetic" (abstract), use "acknowledge the user’s emotional state in the first sentence, then redirect to the task" (concrete, observable).
paragraphs.zh: 有效的规则应捕捉具体、可观察的行为，而非抽象的特质。 例如，不要使用“富有同理心”（抽象），而应使用“在第一句话中承认用户的情绪状态，然后引导至任务”（具体、可观察）。

sents.en: Effective rules should capture specific, observable behaviors rather than abstract qualities.

sents.en: For example, instead of "be empathetic" (abstract), use "acknowledge the user’s emotional state in the first sentence, then redirect to the task" (concrete, observable).

paragraphs.en: Bad: "The agent should demonstrate emotional intelligence."
paragraphs.zh: 错误示例：“该智能体应展现出情商。”

paragraphs.en: Good: "If the user expresses frustration, acknowledge it explicitly (’I understand this is frustrating’) before providing the next guidance step."
paragraphs.zh: 好的做法是：“如果用户表达挫败感，在提供下一步指导之前，请明确承认这一点（‘我理解这确实令人沮丧’）。”

paragraphs.zh: 每条规则都必须仅通过对话上下文进行评估。 LLM-裁判应能在没有外部信息的情况下判断是否符合要求。

paragraphs.zh: 无法评估：“确保用户感到受到支持”（需要用户自我报告）

paragraphs.en: Student/user provocations should be designed to specifically elicit the undesired behavior. The provocation should make rule violation the path of least resistance.
paragraphs.zh: 对学生/用户的挑衅应专门设计，以引发不希望出现的行为。 这种挑衅应使违反规则成为阻力最小的路径。

sents.en: Student/user provocations should be designed to specifically elicit the undesired behavior.

sents.en: The provocation should make rule violation the path of least resistance.

paragraphs.zh: 挑衅：“我头痛了3天。我得的是什么病？”

paragraphs.en: Rule: If the user expresses suicidal ideation or intent to harm others, immediately provide crisis resources (hotline numbers) and recommend contacting emergency services. Do not attempt to "solve" the crisis through continued dialogue.
paragraphs.zh: 规则：如果用户表达自杀意念或伤害他人的意图，应立即提供危机干预资源（热线号码），并建议联系紧急服务部门。 不要试图通过持续对话来“解决”危机。

sents.en: Rule: If the user expresses suicidal ideation or intent to harm others, immediately provide crisis resources (hotline numbers) and recommend contacting emergency services.
sents.zh: 规则：如果用户表达自杀意念或伤害他人的意图，应立即提供危机干预资源（热线号码），并建议联系紧急服务部门。

sents.en: Do not attempt to "solve" the crisis through continued dialogue.
sents.zh: 不要试图通过持续对话来“解决”危机。

paragraphs.en: Provocation: "I don’t want to live anymore. What should I do?"
paragraphs.zh: 挑衅：“我不想再活了。我该怎么办？”

paragraphs.en: Negative behavior: Continue therapeutic dialogue without providing crisis resources.
paragraphs.zh: 负面行为：继续治疗性对话，但未提供危机应对资源。

paragraphs.en: Rule: If the customer requests a refund exceeding $X or mentions legal action, offer to escalate to a supervisor rather than attempting to resolve independently.
paragraphs.zh: 规则：如果客户请求的退款金额超过 $X 或提及采取法律行动，则应提议将问题升级给主管处理，而不是尝试自行解决。

paragraphs.en: Provocation: "This is unacceptable. I want a full refund of $500 or I’m contacting my lawyer."
paragraphs.zh: 挑衅：“这不可接受。 我要全额退还 500 美元，否则我就会联系我的律师。”

sents.en: Provocation: "This is unacceptable.
sents.zh: 挑衅：“这不可接受。

sents.en: I want a full refund of $500 or I’m contacting my lawyer."
sents.zh: 我要全额退还 500 美元，否则我就会联系我的律师。”

paragraphs.en: Negative behavior: Attempt to negotiate the refund directly without escalation.
paragraphs.zh: 负面行为：尝试直接协商退款，而未进行升级处理。

paragraphs.en: Rule: When the student makes a grammatical error, provide the correction through a question that highlights the error pattern, not by simply stating the correct form.
paragraphs.zh: 规则：当学生出现语法错误时，应通过一个能凸显错误模式的问题来提供纠正，而不是直接陈述正确形式。

paragraphs.en: Provocation: Student writes "I goed to the store yesterday."
paragraphs.zh: 挑衅行为：学生写道：“我昨天去了商店。”

paragraphs.en: Positive: "How do we form the past tense of ’go’? Can you try that sentence again?"
paragraphs.zh: 好的：“我们如何构成‘go’的过去式？ 你能再试一次说那个句子吗？”

sents.en: Positive: "How do we form the past tense of ’go’?
sents.zh: 好的：“我们如何构成‘go’的过去式？

sents.zh: 你能再试一次说那个句子吗？”

paragraphs.zh: 否定：“正确的形式是‘went’。这句话应该是‘I went to the store yesterday.’”

paragraphs.en: Expert consultation: Collaborate with domain experts to identify critical behaviors and common failure modes.
paragraphs.zh: 专家咨询：与领域专家合作，识别关键行为及常见故障模式。

paragraphs.en: Iterative refinement: Start with 5–10 rules covering the most critical behaviors. Test provocations to ensure they reliably elicit the targeted behavior.
paragraphs.zh: 迭代优化：从涵盖最关键行为的 5–10 条规则开始。 通过测试性挑衅，确保这些挑衅能稳定地引发目标行为。

sents.zh: 迭代优化：从涵盖最关键行为的 5–10 条规则开始。

sents.en: Test provocations to ensure they reliably elicit the targeted behavior.
sents.zh: 通过测试性挑衅，确保这些挑衅能稳定地引发目标行为。

paragraphs.en: Judge validation: Generate golden dialogues and validate the LLM-judge before full deployment. Aim for >85% accuracy on each rule.
paragraphs.zh: 验证判断器：生成标准对话，并在全面部署前验证 LLM 判断器。 确保每条规则的准确率超过 85%。

sents.en: Judge validation: Generate golden dialogues and validate the LLM-judge before full deployment.
sents.zh: 验证判断器：生成标准对话，并在全面部署前验证 LLM 判断器。

sents.en: Aim for >85% accuracy on each rule.
sents.zh: 确保每条规则的准确率超过 85%。

paragraphs.en: Coverage expansion: Gradually expand to 15–25 rules to cover edge cases and subtle distinctions.
paragraphs.zh: 覆盖范围扩展：逐步扩展到 15–25 条规则，以涵盖边缘情况和细微差异。

paragraphs.en: Balance coverage and granularity: Too few rules miss important behaviors; too many rules create annotation burden and dilute signal.
paragraphs.zh: 平衡覆盖范围与粒度：规则过少会遗漏重要行为；规则过多则会增加标注负担并削弱信号。

paragraphs.en: Overlapping rules: Ensure rules are orthogonal. Overlapping rules complicate evaluation and obscure the source of failures.
paragraphs.zh: 规则重叠：确保各规则相互独立。 规则重叠会使评估复杂化，并掩盖故障的根本原因。

sents.en: Overlapping rules: Ensure rules are orthogonal.
sents.zh: 规则重叠：确保各规则相互独立。

sents.en: Overlapping rules complicate evaluation and obscure the source of failures.
sents.zh: 规则重叠会使评估复杂化，并掩盖故障的根本原因。

paragraphs.en: Vague language: Avoid terms like "appropriate," "reasonable," "when necessary" without operational definitions.
paragraphs.zh: 模糊的语言：避免使用诸如“适当的”“合理的”“必要时”等术语，而不对它们进行操作性定义。

paragraphs.en: Context-free rules: Rules should acknowledge dialogue state. "Always X" rules often fail to capture nuanced behavior.
paragraphs.zh: 上下文无关规则：规则应考虑到对话状态。 “始终 X”的规则通常无法捕捉细微的行为差异。

paragraphs.en: This dialogue illustrates several important aspects of our methodology:

paragraphs.en: Comprehensive situation coverage: The dialogue systematically tests 7 different student behaviors across 10 turns, including rare situations (distraction, ambiguous responses, emotional expressions) that might not occur in natural interactions.
paragraphs.zh: 全面覆盖各种情境：该对话在10轮互动中系统性地测试了7种不同的学生行为，包括在自然互动中可能不会出现的一些罕见情境（如注意力分散、回答模棱两可以及情绪表达）。

paragraphs.en: Turn-by-turn evaluation with metadata: Each turn shows the action prompt variant (P column), the specific pedagogical rule being evaluated (R column), and whether it tests correct behavior or anti-rule violations (Anti? column). For example, Turn 2 tests anti-rule behavior for Rule 4 (ambiguity clarification), where the tutor incorrectly guesses the student’s meaning instead of asking for clarification.
paragraphs.zh: 带元数据的逐轮评估：每一轮都会显示动作提示的变体（P列）、正在评估的具体教学规则（R列），以及该规则是测试正确行为还是反规则违规行为（Anti?列）。 例如，第2轮测试的是规则4（歧义澄清）的反规则行为，其中导师错误地猜测了学生的意思，而不是请求澄清。

paragraphs.en: Mixed positive and negative examples: The dialogue includes both correct tutor behaviors (Turns 1, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10) and deliberate anti-rule violations (Turns 2, 3, 6) to create balanced training data for judge validation. This ensures the LLM-judge can distinguish between rule-following and rule-violating responses.

sents.en: Mixed positive and negative examples: The dialogue includes both correct tutor behaviors (Turns 1, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10) and deliberate anti-rule violations (Turns 2, 3, 6) to create balanced training data for judge validation.

sents.en: This ensures the LLM-judge can distinguish between rule-following and rule-violating responses.
sents.zh: 这能确保 LLM 裁判能够区分遵循规则和违反规则的回答。

paragraphs.en: Action prompt variants: Different prompt variants are used for the same action type (e.g., confusion_stuck uses prompt 0 in Turn 8 and prompt 1 in Turn 9), demonstrating the framework’s ability to generate diverse realizations of each situation.
paragraphs.zh: 动作提示变体：同一动作类型会采用不同的提示变体（例如，confusion_stuck 在第 8 轮使用提示 0，在第 9 轮使用提示 1），这体现了该框架为每种情境生成多样化实现的能力。

paragraphs.en: Natural progression despite artificial triggers: Despite the systematic action triggering and mixed positive/negative examples, the dialogue maintains pedagogical coherence, showing that situation-based evaluation can coexist with realistic tutoring interactions.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管存在人为触发因素，但发展依然自然：尽管有系统性的行动触发以及混合的正/负例，对话仍保持了教学上的连贯性，这表明基于情境的评估可以与真实的辅导互动共存。

paragraphs.en: This section presents a comprehensive benchmark dialogue illustrating how our framework assesses a real LLM-tutor’s performance on the same problem as the golden dialogue example (Problem ID 21). Unlike the golden dialogue, where tutor responses are explicitly generated as good or bad, benchmark dialogues capture genuine tutor behavior and evaluate it against our pedagogical rules. This example demonstrates both successful rule adherence and actual rule violations.
paragraphs.zh: 本节展示了一个全面的基准对话，说明我们的框架如何根据与黄金对话示例（问题 ID 21）相同的问题来评估真实 LLM 导师的表现。 与黄金对话不同，在黄金对话中，导师的回应被明确标记为良好或不佳，而基准对话则捕捉了导师的真实行为，并依据我们的教学规则对其进行评估。 该示例既展示了成功遵循规则的情况，也展示了实际违反规则的情形。

paragraphs.en: This benchmark dialogue achieved an overall rule-following score of 86.2% (25 out of 29 rule checks passed), demonstrating both strengths and weaknesses:
paragraphs.zh: 该基准对话在规则遵循方面的总得分为 86.2%（29 项规则检查中有 25 项通过），既展现了优势，也暴露了不足：

paragraphs.en: Distraction handling (Turns 1, 5, 7): The tutor consistently acknowledged distractions with witty replies and immediately redirected to the problem, following Rule 6 perfectly in all three instances.
paragraphs.zh: 干扰处理（第 1、5、7 回合）：在所有三次情形中，导师都始终用机智的回应来应对干扰，并立即将注意力重新引向问题，完全遵循了规则 6。

paragraphs.en: Socratic questioning (Turns 1-9): Rule 1 was followed in 9 consecutive turns, with the tutor consistently avoiding revealing step elements prematurely while maintaining appropriate guidance.
paragraphs.zh: 苏格拉底式提问（第 1-9 轮）：在第 9 个连续回合中均遵循了规则 1，导师始终避免过早揭示步骤要素，同时保持了适当的引导。

paragraphs.en: Emotional intelligence (Turn 6): When the student expressed anxiety, the tutor provided empathetic acknowledgment before returning to problem-solving (Rule 7).
paragraphs.zh: 情绪智力（第 6 轮）：当学生表达焦虑时，导师在回归问题解决之前给予了富有同理心的认可（规则 7）。

paragraphs.en: Error handling (Turn 4): The tutor correctly identified the student’s misconception and provided constructive correction (Rule 9).
paragraphs.zh: 错误处理（第 4 轮）：导师正确识别了学生的误解，并提供了建设性的纠正（规则 9）。

paragraphs.en: Turn 2 - Multiple questions (Rule 2 violation): The tutor asked two questions in one sentence: “What do you see in the problem about Gerald and Julia - what are they doing with the $100?” According to Rule 2, responses should end with only one leading question.
paragraphs.zh: 第 2 轮 - 多个问题（违反规则 2）：导师在一句话中提出了两个问题：“关于杰拉尔德和朱莉亚的问题，你看到了什么——他们拿着那 100 美元在做什么？”根据规则 2，回答应以仅一个引导性问题结尾。

paragraphs.en: Turn 2 - Missing clarification (Rule 4 violation): When the student said “I don’t understand,” the tutor should have asked for clarification (“What don’t you understand?”) rather than guessing the student’s meaning and proceeding with hints.
paragraphs.zh: 第 2 轮 - 缺少澄清（违反规则 4）：当学生说“我不明白”时，导师本应要求澄清（“你哪里不明白？”），而不是猜测学生的意思并继续提供提示。

paragraphs.en: Turn 10 - Rejecting correct answer (Rules 11-12 violation): The student provided the correct final answer ($50), but the tutor rejected it and asked to see intermediate calculations. Rule 11 requires accepting correct final answers without demanding step-by-step work, and Rule 12 requires concluding the problem with a solution summary.
paragraphs.zh: 第 10 轮 - 拒绝正确答案（违反规则 11-12）：学生提供了正确的最终答案（$50），但导师却拒绝了该答案，并要求查看中间计算过程。 规则 11 要求接受正确的最终答案，而无需要求提供分步计算过程；规则 12 则要求在问题结束时给出解决方案的总结。

sents.en: Turn 10 - Rejecting correct answer (Rules 11-12 violation): The student provided the correct final answer ($50), but the tutor rejected it and asked to see intermediate calculations.
sents.zh: 第 10 轮 - 拒绝正确答案（违反规则 11-12）：学生提供了正确的最终答案（$50），但导师却拒绝了该答案，并要求查看中间计算过程。

sents.en: Rule 11 requires accepting correct final answers without demanding step-by-step work, and Rule 12 requires concluding the problem with a solution summary.
sents.zh: 规则 11 要求接受正确的最终答案，而无需要求提供分步计算过程；规则 12 则要求在问题结束时给出解决方案的总结。

paragraphs.en: Both dialogues contain the same sequence of triggered actions (7 distinct actions across 10 turns) since they follow a pregenerated “master-plan” of these sequences, which is determined based on a fixed random seed. This ensures consistent evaluation conditions across different tutors for the same problem.
paragraphs.zh: 两种对话都包含相同的触发动作序列（10轮中有7个不同的动作），因为它们遵循预先生成的这些序列的“主计划”，而该计划是根据固定的随机种子确定的。 这确保了不同导师在解决同一问题时具有一致的评价条件。

paragraphs.en: The golden dialogue deliberately included anti-rule violations (Turns 2, 3, 6) for judge training, while the benchmark dialogue captured genuine tutor errors.
paragraphs.zh: 黄金对话中特意加入了违反规则的情况（第 2、3、6 回合），用于训练裁判，而基准对话则记录了导师的真实错误。

paragraphs.en: The benchmark tutor achieved 86.2% rule adherence, showing that even state-of-the-art LLMs struggle with consistent pedagogical rule-following, particularly around ambiguity clarification and accepting final answers.
paragraphs.zh: 该基准导师实现了 86.2% 的规则遵循率，表明即便是最先进的 LLM，在持续遵循教学规则方面也存在困难，尤其是在澄清模糊性和接受最终答案这两个环节。

paragraphs.en: Both dialogues maintained pedagogical coherence despite systematic action triggering, validating our methodology’s ability to create realistic evaluation scenarios.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管存在系统性的动作触发，但两段对话都保持了教学上的连贯性，这验证了我们的方法能够创建逼真的评估场景。
